item.title: Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigns after allegations of improper conduct
item.description:
U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio unveil a plaque at the Greek foreign ministry in Athens on Oct. 7, 2026. Mark Schiefelbein/AFP via Getty Images The United States is down one more ambassador. On Oct. 13, 2026, it emerged that President Donald Trump had asked Kimberly Guilfoyle, a MAGA loyalist and ex-fiancée of Trump’s son Donald Jr., to resign her position as U.S. ambassador to Greece , a NATO ally. It follows allegations that the Trump adviser turned diplomat pushed for a Republican donor to pay off her six-figure American Express bill . Guilfoyle later confirmed that she would comply with the request and resigned . In so doing, Athens became one of a number of U.S. overseas missions with a vacancy at the top. item.title: Brazil to shorten workweek in win for Lula ahead of runoff
item.description:
Congress approves constitutional amendment that bans six-day workweeks, which could effect up to 30 million Brazil’s congress has approved a constitutional amendment to shorten the working week to a maximum of 40 hours, a move that could affect 30 million workers and that will hand a political victory to the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ahead of the presidential runoff in under two weeks. In an attempt to overturn the first-round lead secured by his opponent, far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula has strongly championed the amendment, which will give some workers an extra day off each week. item.title: North Korea tests two submarine-launched missiles, state media reports
item.description:
North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles on Wednesday, state media KCNA reported Thursday, saying the launches posed no threat to neighbouring countries. The tests follow heightened tensions with South Korea after a September 21 landmine explosion in the Demilitarised Zone injured three South Korean soldiers.

item.description:

Police responded with water ⁠cannon and teargas to disperse protesters who started a fire at the ministry of education building, overturned bins and smashed the fronts of local businesses. item.description:
Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi national employed as an OpenAI engineer, looks behind a television where a recording device had been placed in a conference room. DOJ/Reuters Abdulrahman Alfozan loved Saudi Arabia. One day before arresting the former OpenAI engineer on charges of bugging the office , the Justice Department worried he would flee back to his home country. Alfozan, his wife, and another family member had already booked one-way tickets, the department said in a court filing. It wouldn't be unusual for Alfozan's thoughts to return to the Gulf. The idea of moving back had followed him through his years working in tech. item.title: Houthis launch fresh wave of missiles across Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Civilians warned to leave target area near Sana’a before attacks as conflict between Riyadh and Houthi forces escalates Saudi Arabia has launched a series of strikes on a strategic oil depot on the outskirts of Yemen’s capital, Sana’a, while later on Tuesday it said it had intercepted missiles launched toward Dharan, location of the headquarters of the huge national energy company Saudi Aramco. The attacks on both sides were a fresh escalation of the conflict between Riyadh and the Iran-backed Houthi forces. Before its offensive on Tuesday, a Saudi spokesperson warned civilians to leave the target area, in an apparent attempt to strike fear into the local population before the biggest attack so far on Houthi energy infrastructure. item.title: White House spokesperson Katie Zacharia’s law career faces scrutiny
item.description:
Photo Illustration by Eric Faison/The Daily Beast/Reuters/Linkedin White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is facing fresh scrutiny about her dubious claims about her career background — and even her explanation for things isn’t adding up. Zacharia, 41, has claimed on her resume that she has worked as an attorney, but there is no evidence that she has passed the bar in any U.S. state, let alone her native California, where she claims to have done legal work. When pressed about her credentials on her second day on the job, she did not appear to name a state, instead saying she passed it “when I moved to China.” Read more at The Daily Beast.

item.title: How Starlink disruptions affected Ukraine's battlefield operations
item.description:
Ukraine is heavily reliant on Starlink for military operations. Inna Varenytsia/REUTERS Ukrainian officials said on Wednesday that Kyiv's access to Starlink has been disrupted. Slower-than-normal speeds have affected military operations, the officials said. Ukraine is heavily reliant on Starlink, specifically for communications and drone missions. Ukraine's access to Starlink internet service was suddenly disrupted for unknown reasons, interfering with military operations, sources in the country's defense ministry and a top presidential advisor said Wednesday morning. Serhii Beskrestnov, a top advisor to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said in a social media post that Elon Musk's SpaceX had implemented speed limits for Starlink terminals overnight. item.title: Fraternity culture under scrutiny in wake of Cornell allegations
item.description:
Cornell University will ban parties and social events at fraternity houses until the end of the academic year, its president said on Tuesday, responding to the outcry over an alleged gang rape on ‌campus in 2024. The measure is the strongest reaction yet from Cornell's leadership to a lawsuit ⁠filed by a former undergraduate, Jane Doe, alleging seven men sexually assaulted her during a party. Over the last several weeks, the Ivy League school in Ithaca, New York, and its ‌president, Michael Kotlikoff, have come under heavy criticism over its response to ⁠the allegations.

item.title: Iran-backed Houthis strike Saudi oil company Aramco's headquarters, officials say
item.description:
Iran-backed Houthi fighters reportedly hit the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s national oil company in overnight strikes, stoking a conflict that risks spiralling into a wider war. The attacks follow a Houthi onslaught that killed 13, injured hundreds, and forced Riyadh’s airport to shut at least through Saturday, denting the kingdom’s reputation for stability and piling pressure on the country’s de facto ruler . Analysts fear the conflict could expand beyond the Arabian Peninsula: The Houthis are reportedly building an advanced missile using Chinese parts. US President Donald Trump has accused the group of “ purposefully trying to drive up Oil Prices ” ahead of November’s midterm elections; Tehran is reportedly targeting crude tankers in a bid to keep prices elevated. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

item.title: Bank of America fined $1.2bn for money-laundering failures
item.description:
The Treasury Department on Tuesday announced more than $1.2 billion in penalties against Bank of America for years of failures to report suspicious transactions and address shortcomings in its anti-money-laundering program. Why it matters: The action includes the third-largest penalty in Treasury history. What they're saying: "Today's actions send a clear message that even the biggest financial institutions are not above the law," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a press release . The big picture: The civil action comes less than a week after federal regulators fined American Express $350 million over similar failures to detect and report suspected money laundering. Zoom in: Bank of America admitted to willfully violating federal anti-money-laundering laws — including requirements to maintain adequate safeguards and report suspicious transactions.
